verdicts.claim: Personal LinkedIn profiles get roughly 5-10x the organic reach of company pages, with median engagement ~4.7% vs 1-2%, per Sprout Social's Q1 2026 Index of 52M+ posts.
verdicts.evidence: Neither stated source supports this. digitalapplied.com says '5 to 8x' engagement (not 5-10x reach) and explicitly does NOT cite Sprout Social — it attributes the figure to unnamed 'multiple independent analyses' with no traceable source. meet-lea.com says personal profiles get '70% more organic reach' (not 5-10x) and never mentions Sprout Social or a 52M+ post study. Checked Sprout Social's own site directly: sproutsocial.com/insights/data/ lists all its published reports (2025 Sprout Social Index, Social Intelligence Report, etc.) — there is no 'Q1 2026 Index' and no 52M+ post study. sproutsocial.com/insights/linkedin-engagement-rate/ cites Social Insider's June 2025 data (5.19% avg engagement) for its LinkedIn benchmarks, not this claim's figures. The '4.7% vs 1-2%' figure only surfaced in AI search-summary text that itself appears to be circulating fabricated/hallucinated 'Sprout Social Q1 2026 Index' stats (a near-identical, obviously fabricated block of stats about '127% more comments... 8.3 million company pages' appeared verbatim across unrelated queries, indicating SEO content-mill contamination, not a real report).
verdicts.corrected: No 'Sprout Social Q1 2026 Index' of 52M+ posts exists per Sprout Social's own report archive. The two cited blogs give different, uncited numbers (5-8x engagement per digitalapplied.com; 70% more reach per meet-lea.com), neither attributed to Sprout Social.

verdicts.claim: LinkedIn's algorithm assigns a profile a 'Topic DNA' and temporarily suppresses reach when new posts don't match established topic history; effect is described as temporary/recoverable with consistent on-topic posting, not permanent.
verdicts.evidence: Fetched both cited pages directly: contentin.io/blog/linkedin-algorithm-2025-the-complete-content-format-strategy-guide contains no mention of 'Topic DNA' or topic-mismatch suppression anywhere. growleads.io/blog/linkedin-algorithm-2026-text-vs-video-reach likewise contains no mention of 'Topic DNA' or suppression/recovery mechanics. A related concept ('Topic Authority'/topic clustering) does exist in unrelated third-party sources (e.g. a Substack post citing Richard van der Blom's report and 'Saywhat's Q1 2026 analysis') — but that source is not one of the two cited, uses different terminology, is not LinkedIn primary documentation, and actually describes the effect as potentially permanent absent 're-anchoring' ('deprioritised out[right]... without intervention'), contradicting the claim's 'temporary/recoverable, not permanent' framing.
verdicts.corrected: Neither cited source discusses 'Topic DNA' at all. A similar but differently-named mechanism appears in other, uncited SEO/consultant blogs, and those sources describe it as potentially permanent rather than reliably temporary.

verdicts.claim: 2-5 LinkedIn posts/week is the reach inflection point (+1,182 impressions/post vs 1x/week), with no evidenced upper-frequency penalty; document/carousel posts average 6.6-7.0% engagement, the highest of any format.
verdicts.evidence: The posting-frequency half is CONFIRMED verbatim: buffer.com/resources/how-often-to-post-on-linkedin states 2-5 posts/week yields '+1,182 more impressions per post' vs weekly posting, explicitly says 'LinkedIn doesn't cap your reach or punish you for posting often,' and is based on '2 million posts from 94,000+ LinkedIn accounts.' However, the format-engagement half is REFUTED: growwithghost.io/blog/linkedin-post-formats-ranked-text-vs-carousel-vs-video-vs-polls-2026 gives Document Posts = 6.1% (below the claimed 6.6-7.0% range) and Carousel Posts = 7.8% (above the claimed range) — neither format actually falls in '6.6-7.0%'. Nor is carousel/document 'the highest of any format': Polls score 8.4% in that same source, higher than carousels (the source caveats poll engagement as low-quality/vote-driven, but the claim's 'highest of any format' statement is still literally false against its own cited source). buffer.com gives only relative multipliers for carousels (e.g. '278% more than videos'), not the 6.6-7.0% figure at all.
verdicts.corrected: Posting-frequency inflection point and 'no penalty' claim confirmed via buffer.com. But per growwithghost.io, Document posts = 6.1%, Carousel = 7.8%, Polls = 8.4% (highest) — the stated 6.6-7.0% range and 'highest of any format' claim do not match the source.

verdicts.claim: DTC/ecommerce founder culture concentrates on X ('DTC Twitter,' build-in-public norms, multiple curated founder-follow lists) with no comparable named LinkedIn equivalent found.
verdicts.evidence: The positive half is confirmed: resources.storetasker.com/12-dtc-founders-to-follow-on-twitter explicitly frames its list around founders 'building in public' and sharing 'the ups... just as much as the downs'; triplewhale.com/blog/dtc-people-on-twitter (confirmed via search cache after a direct 403) is a real, similarly-framed '10 DTC People to Follow on Twitter' list. This corroborates a genuine 'DTC Twitter' follow-list genre. The negative half ('no comparable named LinkedIn equivalent found') is an absence claim that can't be conclusively verified by search — a spot search turned up general multi-platform 'ecommerce leaders to follow' lists (Shopify, Elastic Path, Relo App) that include LinkedIn-profile links among others, but no list specifically branded '[N] DTC Founders to Follow on LinkedIn' analogous to the Twitter ones. Consistent with, but not proof of, the claim.
verdicts.corrected: unable to conclusively confirm or refute the 'no equivalent found' half; treat as unverified rather than established.

verdicts.claim: Tabletop/crowdfunding creator community infrastructure is BoardGameGeek, Discord, Reddit, and Facebook — BackerKit's own creator roadmap omits LinkedIn as a community hub.
verdicts.evidence: Direct WebFetch of the BackerKit URL returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked), and archive.org is not fetchable in this environment, so this relies on two independent WebSearch retrievals of the indexed page content, which agreed: the BackerKit community page recommends Facebook tabletop groups and Reddit tabletop/RPG/board-game subreddits, and funnels creators to BackerKit's own Discord server — no mention of LinkedIn in either retrieval. BackerKit's broader site independently confirms deep, longstanding BoardGameGeek integration (a co-branded 'BoardGameGeek Artist Series' hosted on BackerKit, and project pages that direct backers to rate/review games on BGG as 'the go-to industry hotspot for reviews'), supporting BGG as part of the named infrastructure even though it wasn't the point of the specific community sub-page checked.
verdicts.corrected: confirmed as stated, with the caveat that verification relied on indexed search snippets rather than a direct page fetch since backerkit.com blocked direct WebFetch with a 403.

verdicts.claim: External links placed in a LinkedIn post body reduce reach, but the magnitude is contested — blog estimates of ~60% conflict with LinkedIn's own Senior Director of Product publicly denying any algorithmic link penalty exists.
verdicts.evidence: Both cited sources fail to support the specific claim as sourced. gromming.com/blog/linkedin-external-links-penalty cites a 40-50% impression reduction (per Richard van der Blom's 2025 report) — not ~60% — and contains no mention of any LinkedIn Senior Director denial. writio.ai/blog/how-linkedin-algorithm-changed-2026-what-to-do cites a 30-50% reduction attributed only to unnamed 'high-volume LinkedIn creators tracking their own analytics' — also not ~60%, and also no mention of an official denial. Independent search does confirm a real, similar underlying fact from other sources: LinkedIn's Senior Director of Product Management (Rishi Jobanputra) has publicly stated there's no intentional algorithmic link penalty (reported via a Matt Navarra/Threads repost referencing an actual LinkedIn post), and a separate 900K-post study (tryordinal.com) found an observed gap widening to 42% by 2025 despite that denial — so 'contested magnitude vs. official denial' is directionally true in reality, but not via the two sources cited, and no source anywhere states ~60%.
verdicts.corrected: Real reach-reduction estimates found range 30-50% (not ~60%), and the LinkedIn Senior Director denial is real but is not stated in either cited article — it traces to a separate LinkedIn post reported by industry commentator Matt Navarra.
